title: Thanks, Easter Bunny! Bock Bock!
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss Easter's history and traditions. They cover why Easter's date varies (the Paschal moon, the ecclesiastical moon, the vernal equinox, and the Julian vs. Gregorian calendars), its pagan roots and the claimed link to the goddess Ostara and the Easter Bunny, and the Easter season (Lent, Shrove Tuesday, Ash Wednesday, Palm Sunday, Maundy Thursday, Good Friday, Easter Sunday). They also cover Easter eggs and egg dyeing, egg tapping in Bulgaria, Easter egg rolling at the White House, Atlantic City and Fifth Avenue Easter parades, and the Haltwhistle hare pie and bottle kicking tradition in England. The episode ends with a listener mail segment about Japanese pronunciation and matcha tea.

segments.title: Opening banter and Easter closings
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck trade holiday greetings, reminisce about childhood Easter traditions, and note that more stores seem to close on Easter.

segments.title: Date of Easter and the Paschal moon
segments.summary: The hosts explain that Easter can fall between March 22 and April 25, tied to the vernal equinox and the Paschal moon, which is an ecclesiastical moon and not necessarily an astronomical full moon. They also touch on the Julian and Gregorian calendars and the Passover origin.

segments.title: Pagan origins of Easter and the Easter Bunny
segments.summary: Easter's name is linked to the Saxon goddess Eostre, and its roots are traced to older pagan spring rituals and possibly Ishtar. The Easter Bunny is tied to the hare of Ostara, with stories of a hare that turned a wounded bird into a bird-hare that laid eggs.

segments.title: Lent, Shrove Tuesday and Ash Wednesday
segments.summary: Lent is described as a forty-day fast, with Shrove Tuesday as the last day to eat rich foods. Thomas Aquinas's rules on abstaining from meat and animal products are noted. Ash Wednesday starts the fast with ash crosses made from the previous year's palm fronds.

segments.title: Palm Sunday, Maundy Thursday and Good Friday
segments.summary: Palm Sunday commemorates Jesus's entry into Jerusalem. Maundy Thursday is linked to the Norwich market where fishermen sold their wares, and the name comes from the maund basket. Good Friday marks the crucifixion, and the Stations of the Cross are described.

segments.title: Easter Sunday, egg hunts and dyed eggs
segments.summary: Easter Sunday is described as a celebration. The hosts discuss egg hunts with a possible link to Martin Luther, the custom of dyeing eggs red and green, and the hot cross bun tradition.

segments.title: Egg games and Easter customs around the world
segments.summary: Egg tapping in Bulgaria, the grandmother cheek-rubbing custom, and Mexico's confetti egg game are covered. Parades in Atlantic City and Fifth Avenue, and the White House Easter Egg Roll are discussed.

segments.title: Haltwhistle hare pie and bottle kicking
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Haltwhistle tradition, rooted in a legend about a hare that saved a woman from a bull. Villagers eat hare pie and ale is provided, and a bottle kicking rugby-style match is held, run by the Master of the Stow.

segments.title: Listener mail: Japanese pronunciation and matcha
segments.summary: A listener in Kyoto shares notes on Japanese vowel pronunciation, matcha flavored foods, and cherry blossom season. Josh comments on a cherry blossom coffee he tried in Okinawa.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh gives contact information and signs off.
